title: Agent Cognitive Function
definition: A concept that outlines the cognitive functions an AgentNode can perform, such as pattern recognition, logical inference, data processing, and memory storage.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of an agent as a smart machine that can do various tasks like understanding patterns, making decisions, and remembering things.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: An AgentNode's cognitive functions encompass a range of processes, including pattern recognition (classifier), logical inference (reasoner), information storage and retrieval (memory), and content generation (synthesizer).
difficulty_levels.expert: The agent's cognitive functions represent its ability to perform complex computations and adaptive behaviors. These functions provide the intelligence that enables the agent to interact with its environment, learn from experiences, and make decisions. The cognitive functions also connect the agent to a broader system, enabling it to participate in collaborative, intelligent networks.

extra_fields.insight: Agents can be thought of as intelligent systems that perform cognitive functions, such as pattern recognition and logical inference. These functions enable the agent to interact with its environment, learn from experiences, and make decisions.
